title: Brahmasphuta Siddhanta & Bhavana
price: HTML · 2 chapters · not the classical manuscript

chapters.overview: Brahmagupta is the first mathematician to formally define the arithmetic rules of zero (Śūnya) and negative numbers (Ṛṇa). This chapter lays down the foundations of integer arithmetic over the entire number line.

slokas.deva:
धनयोर्धनमृणमृणयोर्धनर्ष्णयोरन्तरं समैक्यं खम् ।
ऋणमृणधनयोर्घातो धनमृणयोर्धनवधो धनं भवति ॥
खगुणो धनमृणमथवा स्वं भवति खखण्डितं खं खम् ।
slokas.translit:
dhanayordhanamṛṇamṛṇayordhanarṣṇayorantaraṃ samaikyaṃ kham |
ṛṇamṛṇadhanayorghāto dhanamṛṇayordhanavadho dhanaṃ bhavati ||
khaguṇo dhanamṛṇamathavā svaṃ bhavati khakhaṇḍitaṃ khaṃ kham |

anvaya.en: The sum of equal positive and negative is zero (Kham)
Zero times a positive or negative is zero
Zero divided by zero is zero (0/0 = 0)

slokas.translation: The sum of positive and negative is their difference; if they are equal it is zero. The product of a positive and a negative is negative. A positive or negative multiplied by zero becomes zero. Zero divided by zero is zero.
slokas.source: स्रोत अपरीक्षित · source unverified — this wording of the zero rules is not in editions/brahmagupta-full-edition.html (whose 18.30–32 is itself marked unverified) or any other text in this repository.

formula.title: Brahmagupta's Laws of Zero
formula.latex: a + (-a) = 0, \quad a \times 0 = 0, \quad \frac{0}{0} = 0, \quad \frac{a}{0} = \text{khaccheda (left as a quantity with zero divisor)}
formula.notes: Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta 18.34–35 gives these rules and leaves a/0 as "khaccheda" — a quantity with zero as divisor — without evaluating it; the name khahara and its reading as an unbounded quantity are Bhāskara II's (Bījagaṇita, 12th c.), which the snippet's label follows. 0/0 = 0 is Brahmagupta's statement; modern algebra leaves 0/0 undefined.

chapters.overview: Contains Brahmagupta's formula for the area of a cyclic quadrilateral (generalizing Heron's formula) and his powerful Bhāvanā composition law for solving second-order Diophantine equations (Pell's equation: Nx² + 1 = y²).

anvaya.en: Four half-sums of the sides (Semiperimeter s)
Product of s diminished by each side
The square root (padam) is the exact area

slokas.translation: The exact area (of a cyclic quadrilateral) is the square root of the product of four sets of half the sum of the sides diminished by each side.
